content.title: Rich DeMuro
content.text: Apple just released a “hidden” iPhone update… and it’s in a place you’ve probably never checked.These are smaller security fixes that can be pushed out faster than major iOS updates. This patches a bug that could let a malicious website get around iPhone’s built-in protections.To find it:Settings > Privacy & Security > Background Security ImprovementsMake sure “Automatically Install” is turned on and let me know if you find it.All reactions:Karen Moore BoisvertRich DeMuro. Seems we all have the same question…..after finding this, even after seeing auto install is already ON, do we click “install”?15Top fanBeverly UerlingOnce you find it, if it hasn’t been installed, are you supposed to go ahead and manually install?9Cheri BoeglinSo- the real question is do we hit that install at the bottom?2David J. WhitneyThey are just continuing a practice that has been in effect since iphone6. Between 2-3 in the morning rotating phones would be unavailable for 10 to 20 minutes. Updates were pushed during that time. This "change" is just an affirmation.Dyana LynnI found it. Now what? Do I manually install even though it is set to 'automatic install'? I am leery about installing it without knowing whether I should or not.5Tina DawYes I found it on my 14 Pro, it's already turned on and there's an added note stating that 26.3.1 was installed yesterday.4Matt RoseboomVerified account I also had auto install on, but had to manually install it.18Top fanJeannine Correa HuffmanYes, I found it. However, I am wondering why, if "Automatically Install" was turned on why did it not automatically install? ￼35Randall L Rikeor too hard to find … my phone told me weeks agoJennifer Pool HopkinsFound it on my 13 pro and auto install is checked…but it hadn’t been installed yet. Who knows to check there?!11
